title: Piezo-resonant tier select replaces 3D staircase contacts
idea: Piezoelectric effect: each tier of a 3D DRAM stack gets a thin AlScN bulk-acoustic resonator in its local wordline-driver enable path, with a tier-unique film thickness (tier-unique resonance). One shared vertical RF drive line carries the frequency of the target tier, so only that tier's resonator builds enough piezo voltage to enable its drivers.
why: Removes the staircase and per-tier decoders that grow with 26+ tiers (periphery ~49%, fact 7; 3D blocker, fact 2); claim 30-50% less tier-addressing area and one shared via instead of N staircase contacts.

title: Pyroelectric tile sensors steer per-tile refresh in memory-on-logic stacks
idea: Pyroelectric effect: a thin HZO pyroelectric sheet in each tier's bonding layer outputs charge proportional to dT/dt over ~1 mm2 tiles, driving an analog integrator that sets each tile's refresh interval directly without ADCs or thermal diodes. Cool tiles refresh at 256 ms while only hot tiles above logic hot spots stay at 32-64 ms.
why: Attacks refresh energy and bandwidth loss (fact 3) that grows when DRAM tiers sit on hot logic in 3D; claim 2-4x less refresh than worst-case whole-die timing.

title: Magnetostrictive-piezo laminate receivers replace TSVs in memory stacks
idea: Magnetostriction: each thinned die carries micro-coils that transmit, and FeGa/AlN magnetoelectric laminate pads that receive. The stray AC field from the die below strains the magnetostrictive layer, and the piezo layer turns that strain into a mV-scale voltage. The laminate's high field-to-voltage gain allows smaller-pitch, higher-bandwidth contactless links than plain inductive coils.
why: Removes TSVs and their keep-out zones (HBM TSV tax ~3x area and 20-30% yield loss, fact 6); claim recovers 15-25% die area and stacks known-good dies with no through-silicon etch.

title: NbO2 Mott-selector over BEOL capacitor for 4F2 cross-point DRAM
idea: Mott insulator-metal transition: a doped NbO2 threshold-switch film is stacked directly on a BEOL MIM capacitor at each wordline/bitline crossing. Only the fully selected cell exceeds the ~1 V Mott threshold and charges; half-selected cells stay insulating. This gives a transistor-free 1S1C cell that can be repeated in 4-8 BEOL tiers over CMOS periphery.
why: Gives 4F2 per tier with no crystalline access transistor (facts 2 and 4); claim 4-8x bits per wafer area. The risk is off-state leakage, which needs a doping-engineered Mott gap.

title: Room-temperature single-electron electrometer at every vertical bitline foot
idea: Coulomb blockade: a sub-3 nm silicon island single-electron transistor, formed by self-limiting fin oxidation, sits at the base of each vertical bitline as a charge electrometer that can resolve ~10 electrons. Lateral 3D tier capacitors can then hold 0.2 fF instead of 5 fF, because the read no longer depends on charge-sharing against a large bitline capacitance.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) that blocks thin 3D tiers (fact 2); claim 20x smaller Cs, so planar tier capacitors become viable.

title: Goto-pair Esaki tunnel latch stacked in one vertical pillar
idea: Interband tunneling (negative differential resistance): two series Si/SiGe Esaki tunnel diodes, grown epitaxially in one vertical pillar, form a bistable Goto-pair storage node. A single surrounding access gate connects that node to the bitline. The result is a static, capacitor-free 4F2 cell held by pA-level tunnel current.
why: Removes both the capacitor (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3); claim 4F2 static density at a few nW per Mb standby, with no refresh bandwidth loss.

title: Wavelength-addressed photoconductive wordlines through vertical light pipes
idea: Photoconductivity: SiN waveguides thread vertically through the 3D stack, and each tier taps them with a micro-ring drop filter tuned to that tier's wavelength. The dropped light switches photoconductive a-Si/IGZO access channels in place of gate metal. Choosing a wavelength picks the tier, and choosing a waveguide picks the row.
why: Removes the tungsten wordline metal (W chokepoint), the staircase and the high-voltage wordline drivers (facts 2, 7 and 10); claim tier count no longer limited by staircase area.

title: Electroformed copper-filament spare vias repair bonded stacks after test
idea: Ion migration (electrochemical metallization): every hybrid-bond interface carries a grid of spare Cu/SiO2 cells. After post-stack test, a forming voltage drives Cu ions into permanent filaments that reroute signals and power around failed bond pads or bad tiers, like antifuses in the third dimension.
why: Raises HBM and 3D stack yield, which loses 20-30% to bond defects (fact 6); claim recovers 10-20 yield points and so lowers cost per good bit.

title: Logic-heat-biased VO2 hysteresis latches in BEOL tiers
idea: Thermal hysteresis: VO2 nano-bridge cross-point tiers are placed on the logic die, whose steady ~60-65 C waste heat parks every bridge inside its doped, widened hysteresis window. A heat pulse sets a bridge metallic, and a small hold bias keeps it there by self-heating. Briefly removing a row's bias resets that row before selective re-set.
why: Turns stacking heat, normally a refresh penalty (fact 3), into the storage bias; claim a capacitor-free BEOL latch at ~4F2 per tier with no refresh.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO stack gives planar tier capacitors k~70
idea: Ferroelectric negative capacitance: an HZO/ZrO2/Al2O3 superlattice is tuned so the ferroelectric layer sits in a stabilized negative-capacitance regime, raising the series stack's effective permittivity toward k~70. Each tier can then use short lateral planar capacitors instead of AR 60-75 pillars.
why: Hits the k~70 escape route from the capacitor wall (fact 1) and lets 3D tiers shrink (fact 2); claim 2-3x Cs per area and ~40% thinner tier pitch.

title: Air-gap NEMS contact switch as zero-leakage 3D access device
idea: Electrostatic pull-in: in each tier, a laterally actuated Ru/TiN nanobeam, released from a sacrificial layer, replaces the lateral access transistor. In the off state a vacuum gap sits in series with the capacitor, so there is no subthreshold leakage tail at all.
why: Removes the ≤13 fA leakage tail that forces refresh (fact 3); claim retention set only by dielectric leakage (minutes), so refresh energy falls ~90%. Contact endurance near 1e15 cycles is the big risk.

title: Avalanche-gain segment amplifies charge at each vertical bitline
idea: Impact ionization: a short vertical p-i-n avalanche section at the foot of each vertical bitline multiplies the charge dumped by a tiny tier capacitor 50-100x before it reaches the sense amp. It works like an avalanche photodiode, but for stored electrons.
why: Lets 3D tiers use 10x smaller capacitors (facts 1 and 2) and shrinks sense-amp periphery (fact 7); claim 10x Cs relief, with excess noise the main risk.

title: Through-silicon infrared beams with retro-modulators replace HBM TSVs
idea: Silicon's infrared transparency: the HBM base die holds InP micro-emitters whose 1.3 µm beams pass straight through thinned silicon dies to Ge photodiodes on each memory die (downlink). For the uplink, each memory die modulates the reflection of a base-die beam with an electro-absorption retro-modulator, so the DRAM dies need no lasers.
why: Removes the TSV tax and its yield loss (fact 6) and cuts movement energy (fact 5); claim <1 pJ/bit vertical links and ~3x less area per bit than TSV HBM.

title: Capillary self-alignment for cheap high-throughput die-to-wafer stacking
idea: Surface tension: hydrophilic bond pads with hydrophobic surroundings, plus a water microdroplet, pull each roughly placed die to <200 nm alignment as the water evaporates, before direct hybrid bonding. Fast, coarse pick-and-place replaces slow precision bonders.
why: Cuts capital and throughput limits of HBM and 3D die stacking (facts 4 and 6); claim 5-10x die-to-wafer throughput per tool, which suits US assembly lines.

title: Kirkendall-hollowed double-wall nanotube capacitors in each tier
idea: Kirkendall effect: lateral Ni or Cu nanowires are deposited in each tier and coated with an oxidizing or sulfiding shell, then annealed. Unequal diffusion hollows each wire into a tube, and both the inner and outer walls become electrode surface without any deep etch.
why: Raises Cs at fixed aspect ratio (fact 1) and avoids AR 60-75 etches in 3D tiers (fact 2); claim ~1.8x capacitor area for the same footprint.

title: Spinodal vertically-aligned nanocomposite pillars as EUV-free 4F2 channels
idea: Spinodal phase separation: a single co-deposited oxide nanocomposite, such as IGZO-matrix/MgO or a ZnO pillar system, self-separates into ~10 nm-pitch vertical semiconductor pillars. A coarse DUV prepattern pins the pillar lattice so the pillars register to wordlines and become vertical channel transistors.
why: Replaces EUV patterning for 4F2 vertical-channel arrays (fact 4); claim removes 3-5 EUV layers, cutting about a quarter of wafer cost.

title: Dielectrophoretic placement of single-crystal nanowires as tier access transistors
idea: Dielectrophoresis: single-crystal Si nanowires are grown off-wafer, suspended in fluid, and pulled by an AC field into electrode gaps in every BEOL tier. Each tier gets crystalline lateral access transistors at <400 C without per-tier epitaxy.
why: Solves the missing lateral transistor in 3D DRAM (fact 2); claim crystalline mobility and low leakage in every tier with a cheap, low-temperature process.

title: Thin-film Peltier bonding layer chills DRAM tiers above logic
idea: Peltier effect: a Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 superlattice thermoelectric layer in the bonding stack between logic and DRAM tiers actively pumps heat downward and doubles as a power-distribution plane. The DRAM tiers stay 20-30 K cooler than the logic.
why: Leakage roughly halves per ~10 K, which attacks refresh (fact 3) and makes memory-on-logic 3D possible; claim 4-8x longer retention, net of Peltier power.

title: 77 K cryogenic stacks let 3D tiers use sub-femtofarad capacitors
idea: Carrier freeze-out of thermal leakage: liquid-nitrogen-cooled 3D DRAM stacks at 77 K cut access-transistor leakage by about 1e6. Lateral tier capacitors of 0.3-0.5 fF then retain data for seconds or more, so planar thin tiers replace high-AR pillars.
why: Breaks the capacitor wall (fact 1) and the 3D blocker (fact 2), and nearly removes refresh (fact 3); claim 10x lower Cs requirement and >100x refresh reduction for datacenter racks.

title: Workfunction charge-plasma junctions for implant-free stacked lateral transistors
idea: Charge-plasma effect: source and drain regions of the lateral access transistors in each deposited channel tier are induced electrostatically by low- and high-workfunction metal contacts, not by dopant implants. No implant has to pass through upper tiers, and no activation anneal is needed.
why: Unblocks the lateral transistor in 3D DRAM (fact 2) and keeps the thermal budget low; claim each tier is processed identically with no implant masks, so mask count does not grow with tier count.

title: LC-resonant paired wordlines recycle charge between adjacent rows
idea: Electrical resonance: adjacent wordlines are paired through a spiral inductor in the bonding layer, so falling-row charge resonantly transfers to the rising row (adiabatic energy recovery) instead of being dumped to ground at each activate.
why: Attacks the stuck CV2 energy of ~3 V wordlines (fact 10); claim 50-70% wordline energy recovery and smaller charge pumps (fact 7).

title: Vacuum-channel field-emission nanotriode as stacked access device
idea: Field emission: each tier's access device is a 10 nm sacrificially formed vacuum gap between a sharp emitter tip and a collector. A gate electrode modulates the Fowler-Nordheim emission, and with zero field the vacuum carries no current at all.
why: Removes the leakage tail (fact 3) with no moving parts, unlike NEMS switches, and is temperature-insensitive for stacking on logic; claim refresh cut by >10x.

title: Monolayer MoS2 channel tiers stacked at 20 nm pitch
idea: Quantum confinement: atomically thin MoS2 channels, MOCVD-grown at <450 C, have a ~2 eV confined bandgap that suppresses off-state tunneling and thermionic leakage about 1000x versus silicon. Because each channel is only 0.7 nm thick, tiers can stack at ~20 nm pitch, which makes 50+ tiers practical.
why: Shrinks tier pitch and leakage at once (facts 2 and 3); claim 3D break-even reached at lower stack height and 10x longer retention.

title: Pyroelectric heat-pulse non-destructive read of stacked ferroelectric tiers
idea: Pyroelectric effect: in a 3D-stacked HZO ferroelectric capacitor array, a nanosecond current pulse in a resistive heater line beside each row warms the cells by a few kelvin. Each cell then emits a pyroelectric current whose sign gives its polarization, so the read never switches the cell and the data is non-volatile with no write-back.
why: Removes the destructive read and write-back (fact 8) and the endurance drain of FeRAM reads; claim read energy cut ~5x, with cycling wear only on writes.

title: Straintronic nanomagnets switched by a shared piezo wordline film
idea: Magnetostriction: each non-volatile bit is a FeGa or Co nanomagnet sitting on an AlScN piezo film that forms the wordline. A voltage pulse on the film strains the row's magnets past their anisotropy barrier, a bitline bias picks which magnets flip, and an MTJ reads the state. No write current flows.
why: Attacks energy per bit and the voltage floor (fact 10) for non-volatile tiers; claim ~1-10 aJ writes, 100x below STT-MRAM, and stackable BEOL tiers.

title: Vertical BiSb spin-Hall pillar writes MTJs on eight tiers
idea: Spin Hall effect: a vertical bismuth-antimony topological-insulator pillar (no tungsten) threads eight BEOL tiers of perpendicular MTJs. Current in the pillar delivers spin-orbit torque to every MTJ along it, and a voltage-controlled-anisotropy bias on one tier's MTJ chooses which bit actually switches.
why: Gives non-volatile 3D SOT density with one write line per column (fact 2) and avoids the W chokepoint; claim 8x bits per footprint versus planar SOT-MRAM.

title: Persistent-photoconductivity oxide tiers written by through-stack light
idea: Persistent photoconductivity: a UV pulse sent down a vertical light pipe ionizes oxygen vacancies in IGZO/ZnO channel tiers into metastable donors that keep the channel conductive with the power off. A gate bias selects which tier captures the charge, and a positive-gate pulse erases by re-neutralizing the vacancies.
why: Gives non-volatile tiers with no capacitor and no per-tier write drivers (facts 1 and 7); claim days-to-months retention from a single light pipe per column, with the speed-retention trade as the risk.

title: Electrochromic tiers with plasmonic readout for read-mostly AI weights
idea: Electrochromism: WO3 nanocells, colored or bleached by proton intercalation, keep their state with no power. Each cell sits on a plasmonic nanoantenna whose resonance shift a bonded photodiode array reads optically, a whole page in parallel. Writes are slow (µs) but reads are fast, which suits model weights that are written rarely.
why: Takes read-mostly AI weight capacity off DRAM and removes per-read data movement (facts 5 and 8); claim page-parallel optical reads at tens of fJ/bit with non-volatile storage.

title: Few-electron Coulomb-blockade nanodot strings along vertical pillars
idea: Coulomb blockade: a ring of ~2 nm Si nanodots in a thin tunnel oxide along each vertical channel pillar stores 3-10 electrons per bit. Charging energy quantizes the charge state and helps it resist leakage, while the thin barrier allows ~10 ns low-voltage writes. The layout follows 3D NAND, but the low fluence aims at high endurance.
why: Gives a non-volatile 3D cell at DRAM-like speed and lower voltage (facts 2 and 10); claim 3D NAND-class density with 1e10+ cycles, given the tiny charge moved.

title: Layer-transferred InAs/AlSb resonant-tunneling floating-gate tiers
idea: Resonant tunneling: a triple-barrier InAs/AlSb stack passes charge into a floating gate only when ~2.5 V aligns the resonance, and blocks it otherwise, giving very long retention. The III-V layers are grown on cheap substrates, then oxide-bonded as 4 stacked tiers onto CMOS logic.
why: Gives low-voltage, high-endurance non-volatile working memory in 3D (facts 2 and 10); claim sub-fJ writes and >1e7-1e12 endurance, density multiplied by tier count.

title: Lithium-moved Schottky barrier makes selector-free cross-point tiers
idea: Ion migration: a field-driven Li-ion shift at a LixTiO2/metal interface moves a Schottky barrier, so the same junction stores a non-volatile resistance state and rectifies current. Self-rectifying cells allow 4F2 BEOL cross-point tiers with no separate selector layer.
why: Gives 4F2 stacked non-volatile cells without a transistor or selector (facts 2 and 4); claim 2x fewer layers per tier than 1S1R cross-point and cheap BEOL stacking.

title: Spin-crossover molecular tiers with room-temperature-straddling hysteresis loops
idea: Thermal hysteresis: Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover films whose 30-40 K hysteresis loop is engineered to straddle 20-60 C hold either the high-spin or low-spin state with no power. A heater pulse writes high-spin, a field pulse writes low-spin, and the ~10% dielectric or resistance change is the read. The films can be evaporated at <200 C, so many cheap tiers fit in BEOL.
why: Gives non-volatile tiers from molecules with no critical minerals (resource axis, fact 2); claim very low capital per tier. Speed and endurance are unproven.

title: Purely electronic Mott-avalanche switching in lacunar spinel cross-points
idea: Electric-field-driven Mott transition: GaV4S8-family lacunar spinel films switch by an electronic avalanche that collapses the Mott gap, with no ion motion, into a retained metallic filament. Cross-point tiers of these films aim at RRAM-like density without oxygen-vacancy wear.
why: Gives a non-volatile 4F2 stackable cell (fact 2) with ion-free switching for DRAM-class endurance; claim >1e12 cycles in principle. Room-temperature retention is the risk.

title: 1T-TaS2 charge-density-wave hidden-state switching in vdW tiers
idea: Charge density waves: picosecond electrical pulses drive 1T-TaS2 flakes into a metastable hidden CDW state whose resistance differs by orders of magnitude, and a longer pulse restores the ground state. Transferable van der Waals flakes can be stacked as many thin non-volatile tiers.
why: Gives ps-scale switching with non-volatile tiers of atomic thickness (facts 2 and 10); claim fJ writes. Room-temperature stability of the hidden state is speculative.

title: Snap-through bistable buckled nanobeams in released tier cavities
idea: Euler buckling bistability: compressively stressed SiN/TiN nanobeams, released in cavities in each tier, rest bowed up or down. Electrostatic electrodes snap a beam between its two states without any contact, and capacitive sensing reads the position. Zero standby power, and no stiction or contact wear.
why: Gives non-volatile, leakage-free stacked bits with no refresh (fact 3) and no exotic materials; claim fJ-scale snap energy and high endurance because there is no contact.

title: Alpha-In2Se3 ferroelectric-semiconductor channel tiers stacked by the dozen
idea: Interlocked in-plane and out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization: atomically thin α-In2Se3 is both the channel and the ferroelectric. Gate pulses flip its polarization, which non-volatilely shifts channel conduction, and its ~1 nm thickness allows dozens of vdW tiers in vertical strings.
why: Gives a thin non-volatile 3D cell with no capacitor (facts 1 and 2); claim tier pitch <15 nm and 30+ tiers.

title: AlScN wurtzite ferrodiode makes self-rectifying 3D ferroelectric cross-points
idea: Polarization-modulated Schottky barrier: in CMOS-compatible ferroelectric AlScN, deposited at ≤400 C, switching polarization raises or lowers the interface barrier. Each cell is therefore a non-volatile diode that both stores and rectifies, so selector-free cross-point tiers stack over logic.
why: Gives non-volatile 4F2 stacked arrays with very long retention and no access transistor (facts 2 and 4); claim 4-8 tiers in BEOL over periphery.

title: Unipolar VCMA-MTJ with thin-film diode enables stacked cross-point MRAM
idea: Voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy: precessional writes with timed unipolar voltage pulses flip perpendicular MTJs at fJ energy, so each cell needs only a one-way thin-film diode instead of a transistor. Unipolar operation lets 4F2 MRAM cross-point tiers be repeated in BEOL.
why: Brings non-volatile MRAM to 4F2 density in 3D (facts 2 and 4) at near-DRAM speed; claim fJ writes and ~4x density versus 1T1MTJ.

title: Vertical domain-wall racetracks lining deep holes like 3D NAND
idea: Current-induced domain wall motion: Co/Ni multilayer racetracks deposited on the sidewalls of deep vertical holes store 32-64 magnetic domains per hole. A spin-orbit-torque Pt liner shifts the domains to a single read/write MTJ at the hole base.
why: Gives non-volatile storage with many bits per 4F2 footprint and almost no periphery per bit (facts 2 and 7); claim 10-30x density per footprint with ns shifts.

title: Zero-stray-field Mn3Sn antiferromagnetic bits packed at sub-ferromagnetic pitch
idea: Anomalous Hall effect in noncollinear antiferromagnets: Mn3Sn bits switched by spin-orbit torque are read by their large anomalous Hall or tunneling signal. Because antiferromagnets emit no dipolar stray field, neighboring bits and stacked tiers can be packed far tighter than ferromagnetic MTJs without crosstalk.
why: Gives denser non-volatile 3D packing with ps-scale switching (facts 2 and 5); claim ~2x tighter pitch per tier than ferromagnetic MRAM and field-immune bits.

title: BiFeO3 exchange-coupled magnetoelectric tiers via layer transfer
idea: Magnetoelectric exchange coupling: about 100 mV across La-doped BiFeO3 rotates its antiferromagnetic order, which flips an exchange-coupled CoFe magnet read by an MTJ. The BFO is grown at high temperature on donor wafers, then layer-transferred into stacked BEOL tiers.
why: Gives non-volatile bits at sub-volt write voltage (fact 10) with stackable tiers (fact 2); claim aJ-level writes, 10-30x below DRAM CV2.

title: Interfacial phase-change superlattices on vertical-bitline hole sidewalls
idea: Interfacial phase change: an ALD-deposited GeTe/Sb2Te3 superlattice switches by flipping Ge atoms at the interfaces, not by melting, cutting energy ~10x. The superlattice lines the sidewalls of vertical bitline holes crossing horizontal wordline plates, making a VRRAM-style 3D array with a single-mask hole etch.
why: Gives dense non-volatile 3D cells (fact 2) with low capital (fact 4); claim tier count scales like 3D NAND, with 10x lower switching energy than PCM.

title: Built-in-bias antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitors stacked in 1T-nC strings
idea: Field-induced antiferroelectric-ferroelectric transition: ZrO2 capacitors with asymmetric-workfunction electrodes shift the double hysteresis loop so one lobe straddles zero bias, giving two non-volatile states. Antiferroelectric switching fatigues less than true ferroelectrics. Several such capacitors are stacked vertically on one access transistor.
why: Gives non-volatile, high-endurance stacked bits (facts 1 and 2) with n bits per transistor; claim 4-8 bits per access device and >1e12 cycles.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain-wall crossbars in thin-film lithium niobate
idea: Domain-wall conduction: in LNOI wafers, which photonics fabs already make, voltage pulses create or erase conductive domain walls across each nanocell. Reading senses wall current without switching, so the read is non-destructive and the walls persist with no power.
why: Gives a non-volatile cell with non-destructive read (fact 8) and high endurance, stackable by wafer bonding (fact 2); claim >1e10 cycles and selector-friendly on/off >1e3.

title: Deep-trench energy-reserve die flushes stacked DRAM to NV tier
idea: Capacitive energy storage as architecture: each memory stack includes one silicon deep-trench capacitor die holding enough energy (~mJ) to copy every DRAM tier into an on-stack ferroelectric or NAND tier over wide internal buses within ms of power loss. The stack keeps DRAM speed and gains non-volatility.
why: Meets non-volatility without a new cell, keeps DRAM performance, and removes server-level NVDIMM batteries; claim persistent memory for <5% added stack cost.

title: Low-temperature ferroelectric tier licensing for idle US logic fabs
idea: Low-temperature orthorhombic-phase crystallization: HZO and AlScN become ferroelectric at ≤400 C, so non-volatile memory tiers can be added on top of finished logic wafers. A business would license a 'memory-tier kit' (process recipe, compiler, test IP) to US 28-65 nm fabs, turning underused capacity into memory output without a new DRAM fab.
why: Attacks US manufacturability (1-2% share) and capital intensity (fact 4); claim memory output at <10% of greenfield DRAM capex per wafer.
